violations.suggested_fix: For Clozapine Monitoring OSCE, expected answers must include: (1) Clozapine dosing protocol (12.5mg nocte, titrate by 25-50mg every 3-7 days to target 300-450mg/day), (2) Mandatory WBC/neutrophil monitoring (weekly x 18 weeks, fortnightly x 1 year, then monthly), (3) Clozapine cessation criteria (WBC <3.0, neutrophils <1.5), (4) Side effect management (laxatives for constipation, dose reduction for sedation), (5) Clozapine Patient Monitoring Service (CPMS) registration requirement

violations.issue: No PBS authority requirements specified for clozapine
violations.suggested_fix: Clozapine requires PBS authority (treatment-resistant schizophrenia after trial of 2+ antipsychotics). Authority criteria: (1) Diagnosed schizophrenia, (2) Adequate trial of ≥2 antipsychotics (≥6 weeks each at therapeutic dose), (3) Persistent symptoms despite treatment. PBS streamline code for clozapine 100mg: 2933K

Clozapine dosing (Australian standard): Starting 12.5mg nocte, increase by 25-50mg every 3-7 days. Target 300-450mg/day (divided BD/TDS if >200mg). Maximum 900mg/day. Reduce dose by 50% if smoking cessation (CYP1A2 induction removed). Seizure risk increases >600mg/day.

Mandatory monitoring: (1) FBC (WBC, neutrophils, platelets) - weekly x 18 weeks, fortnightly until 1 year, then monthly lifelong, (2) Fasting glucose/HbA1c baseline then 3-monthly (metabolic syndrome risk), (3) Lipid profile baseline then 3-monthly, (4) Weight/BMI/waist circumference monthly, (5) ECG if cardiac risk factors (QTc prolongation, myocarditis risk in first 8 weeks), (6) Troponin/CRP if chest pain/tachycardia (myocarditis surveillance)

violations.issue: No drug interaction assessment for clozapine provided
violations.suggested_fix: Common clozapine interactions: (1) Benzodiazepines - respiratory depression/collapse (avoid or use low doses), (2) Valproate - increases clozapine levels 20-30% (dose reduction may be needed), (3) Fluvoxamine (strong CYP1A2 inhibitor) - increases clozapine levels 5-10x (contraindicated), (4) Ciprofloxacin - increases clozapine levels 30% (avoid or reduce clozapine dose), (5) Smoking cessation - increases clozapine levels 50-100% (reduce dose by 50%)

STOP clozapine immediately if: (1) WBC <3.0 x 10^9/L (red alert), (2) Neutrophils <1.5 x 10^9/L (red alert), (3) Myocarditis suspected (chest pain + elevated troponin/CRP + tachycardia), (4) Agranulocytosis (neutrophils <0.5). NEVER rechallenge if agranulocytosis, myocarditis, or seizures occurred. Yellow alert (WBC 3.0-3.5, neutrophils 1.5-2.0): Twice-weekly FBC, continue clozapine if stable.
